en.name: Frying oil, re-used
en.summary: Strained used frying oil keeps 1 month in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and 6–9 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). It is far shorter-lived than fresh oil, because frying has already partly broken the oil down and left food particles in it.
en.pantry: No room-temperature timeline is given for used frying oil, and leaving the pan on the stove until next time is the habit this record exists to argue against. Frying does three things to an oil: it oxidises it, it hydrolyses it with water from the food, and it leaves crumbs and protein behind. Those crumbs carry on degrading the oil and give spoilage organisms something to work with, and heat accelerates all of it. Strain the oil through muslin or a coffee filter as soon as it is cool enough to handle, into a clean jar, and refrigerate it.
en.fridge: 1 month at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, strained and in a sealed jar. That is a short window compared with a fresh bottle, and it is honest: used oil has a lower smoke point than it started with, darkens faster, and foams and smokes sooner each time it is heated. Cold will make it cloudy or thick, which is harmless. Never pour used oil back into the bottle of fresh oil — the degraded oil accelerates the fresh, and you lose both.
en.freezer: 6–9 months at −18 °C (0 °F) for a strained, sealed jar, which is the right answer if you deep-fry only occasionally. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond that; what runs out is the oil's ability to fry, as oxidation continues slowly even in the cold. Leave headspace in the jar, since oil expands slightly, and label it with what you fried in it — oil used for fish will flavour whatever you cook in it next.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge and let the jar come to room temperature before heating, so no water condenses into the oil; water in hot oil spits violently. Do not try to melt a frozen jar over direct heat.
spoilage: Dark, syrupy oil that smokes at a much lower temperature than it used to.
Heavy foaming around the food as soon as it goes in.
A sharp, rancid or fishy smell, or a smell of whatever was last fried in it.
A sticky, varnish-like film on the jar, which is oxidised oil polymerising.
tips: Strain it through muslin or a coffee filter while it is still warm, not hot.
Label the jar with what was fried in it; fish oil is only good for fish.
Never mix used oil into a bottle of fresh oil.
Discard oil that is dark, syrupy or smoking early, whatever the date says.

faq.q: How many times can you reuse frying oil?
faq.a: There is no fixed number — judge it by colour, smell and behaviour. Dark, syrupy oil that foams and smokes early has had enough, whatever the calendar says.

faq.q: How long does used frying oil keep?
faq.a: 1 month in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 6–9 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F), strained and sealed.

faq.q: Can you mix used frying oil with fresh oil?
faq.a: No. The degraded oil speeds up the breakdown of the fresh oil, so you end up with two lots of poor oil instead of one good one.

zh.name: 回鍋油
zh.summary: 過濾後的回鍋油放 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 1 個月，−18 °C 冷凍是 6～9 個月。它比新油短命得多，因為油炸已經先把油部分分解掉，而且裡面還留著食物碎屑。
zh.pantry: 回鍋油沒有給室溫期限；而「整鍋就擺在爐上等下次再用」這個習慣，正是這一篇存在要反對的事。油炸對油做了三件事：把它氧化、用食物帶來的水把它水解，再留下一堆碎屑和蛋白質。那些碎屑會繼續分解油，也給了腐敗菌可以利用的東西，而溫度會加速這一切。請在油涼到可以處理時就用紗布或濾紙濾進乾淨罐子，然後冷藏。
zh.fridge: 過濾後裝密封罐，放 4 °C 以下 1 個月。和一瓶新油比起來這很短，但那是誠實的：用過的油發煙點已經下降，顏色變深得更快，而且每加熱一次就更早起泡冒煙。低溫會讓它變濁或變稠，那是無害的。絕對不要把回鍋油倒回新油瓶——劣化的油會加速新油的劣化，結果是兩邊一起壞掉。
zh.freezer: 過濾密封後放 −18 °C 下 6～9 個月；如果你只是偶爾油炸，這就是正確答案。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全；先用完的是「還能不能炸」這件事，因為氧化在低溫下依然緩慢進行。罐子要留一點頂空，因為油會微微膨脹；並且標上你炸過什麼——炸過魚的油，會把味道帶進下一鍋任何東西裡。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏解凍，並讓整罐回到室溫再加熱，免得水氣凝進油裡；熱油遇水會爆得很兇。不要把整罐冷凍的油直接放在火上融。
spoilage: 顏色深、質地變得像糖漿，而且在比以前低得多的溫度就開始冒煙。
食材一下鍋就大量起泡。
聞起來刺鼻、油耗，或有魚腥味、上次炸過什麼的味道。
罐子上出現黏黏像亮光漆的膜，那是氧化的油在聚合。
tips: 趁油還溫（不是燙）的時候用紗布或濾紙過濾。
在罐上標明炸過什麼；炸過魚的油只適合再炸魚。
絕對不要把回鍋油混進新油瓶裡。
顏色深、變稠、很早就冒煙的油，不管日期怎麼寫都該丟。

faq.a: 沒有固定次數——用顏色、氣味和表現來判斷。顏色深、變稠、一下鍋就起泡冒煙，就是夠了，不管日曆怎麼說。

faq.q: 用過的炸油可以放多久？
faq.a: 過濾密封後，4 °C 以下冷藏 1 個月，或 −18 °C 冷凍 6～9 個月。

faq.q: 回鍋油可以和新油混在一起嗎？
faq.a: 不行。劣化的油會加速新油分解，結果是兩份差油，而不是一份好油。
